paragraphs: CORTEX SENTINEL
Short Description: A prototype workstation-security companion combining fingerprint authentication, six environment checks and controlled credential use.
Business plan and staged engineering-funding proposal | 14 November 2026
Financial planning period: FY 2027–28 to FY 2036–37, April–March. Prepared by a five-member computer-science team led by Kavyansh Kumar Baghel.
All market estimates and financial projections in this plan are illustrative classroom planning assumptions, not measured market statistics, confirmed orders or promised results.

pages.title: I) ABOUT US – IN BRIEF
paragraphs: YOUR BUSINESS NAME: Cortex Sentinel
YOUR TAGLINE (IF ANY): Identity checked. Environment checked.

Proposed positioning: a visible, locally controlled security workflow for selected sensitive workstations. The product joins fingerprint verification with checks of the surrounding workstation environment before allowing its credential-injection function. It is being developed as a complementary control; it has not been shown to replace Windows authentication, endpoint protection or a firm’s security policies.

The immediate business objective is a teacher-directed request for a staged engineering pilot. The accepted planning envelope is ₹44,470 for ten devices, beginning with two engineering units. No grant, customer or production contract has been secured. The business proceeds towards commercial evaluation only if engineering tests, customer evidence and unit economics justify the next commitment.

subsections.title: What We do
paragraphs: Cortex Sentinel is a student-led prototype combining an ESP32 hardware unit and a Windows/Python application. The team reports fingerprint functions, six pre-flight checks, continuing environment monitoring and TKC credential handling. The actual prototype still needs PCB and other upgrades. A refined working prototype is used as an explicit planning scenario, not as evidence of production readiness.

The retained problem is sensitive corporate workstation access: checking identity at one moment may leave the user with limited visibility into subsequent changes in the environment. Cortex Sentinel intends to make selected checks visible and connect them to credential use. The size and frequency of this problem in target firms still require direct customer evidence.

subsections.title: History & Shareholding
paragraphs: The current project exists at prototype stage; production has not begun. This plan formalizes the next engineering and customer-learning steps. Cortex Sentinel is the approved working name, without a claim of company incorporation, trademark registration or established trading history.

The five named contributors are computer-science majors. Legal ownership, equity allocations, incorporation date, founder capital and intellectual-property arrangements have not been established. These matters must be documented before external investment or commercial contracts.

subsections.title: Services
paragraphs: The intended offering is a hardware unit with a supporting Windows application, followed by software updates and customer support at an estimated ₹500 per year. Gemini/AI functionality and its earlier subscription revenue are excluded. No 24-hour support or unlimited-service commitment is assumed.

subsections.title: Processes
paragraphs: The six current checks cover SSID, BSSID, the USB baseline, process scanning, path/masquerade integrity and final verification. Fingerprint authentication is separate from these six checks. The user-reported monitoring configuration polls Wi-Fi every 10 seconds, USB every 3 seconds and processes every 30 seconds; these are configuration claims, not verified detection times.

Controlled recovery after restart or disconnect is planned: permission to inject credentials is invalidated until fresh fingerprint authentication and all six checks succeed. A failed or disconnected host process cannot be assumed to lock Windows. Device-side gating and Windows locking have different limits. Encrypted persistence and event-history implementation remain deferred.

subsections.title: Vision
paragraphs: Proposed vision: help small professional firms use sensitive workstations with a clearer understanding of who is using them and whether the immediate operating environment has changed.

subsections.title: Mission
paragraphs: Proposed mission: develop and test a practical fingerprint-and-environment-checking companion, explain its limits honestly, and support deployments only where customers identify a useful workflow and the team can deliver it reliably.

For the first planning year, success means documented engineering performance, a validated customer problem and a credible cost model. Commercial growth is conditional on these foundations; it is not measured by an invented market share or an unsupported security claim.

pages.title: II) OUR MARKET
paragraphs: MARKET OVERVIEW & FORECASTING OF OUR INDUSTRY

Cortex Sentinel sits between workstation authentication, credential handling and endpoint-environment monitoring. The relevant customer decision is whether this combined workflow adds enough value alongside existing controls to justify another device, installation effort and continuing support.

The first discovery segment is Gurugram accounting and finance SMEs. Legal firms and small banks remain later candidates. India-wide and worldwide expansion are future ambitions, not dated commitments. ICAI’s September 2026 programme lists professional technology training in Gurugram, supporting the existence of a local professional ecosystem. It does not establish access to buyers or demand for this product. [4]

The market model that follows is a deliberately synthetic classroom planning exercise. Its firm counts, eligible seats and growth assumptions are selected inputs. They are not a survey of Gurugram, an estimate from a market-research publisher or a prediction of sales.

subsections.title: Our Market: Historical Data, Forecasts on growth
paragraphs: A narrow initial model uses 100 potentially eligible firms, five relevant workstations per firm and ₹4,500 assumed device value: 100 × 5 × ₹4,500 = ₹22.50 lakh of illustrative one-time device value. This is a planning denominator only. Eligibility, actual prices, tax basis, replacement cycles and willingness to buy have not been measured.

pages.title: Our Playfield
paragraphs: The customer can address security through several layers. Windows Hello serves sign-in; a FIDO security key serves supported account authentication; endpoint software examines threats and device posture. Cortex Sentinel’s intended role is a narrower visible workflow joining biometric permission, selected environment checks and its own credential function. [1–3]
Graphic/Collage based overview of your industry: identity → workstation and peripherals → credential use → monitoring and response. Customer policy and installation authority surround every layer.

subsections.title: Main complaints of customers: a), b), c)
paragraphs: These are interview hypotheses, not collected complaints: (a) uncertainty about changes in workstation/peripheral conditions; (b) friction in credential and access procedures; (c) concern about recovery, false lockouts and support burden. Interviews must allow customers to report that existing controls are sufficient or that these issues are not important.

pages.title: Market – Historical Data & Forecast
paragraphs: Illustrative baseline sensitivity and forward planning scenario — synthetic, not measured historical market data or a researched forecast. The teacher’s example years and dollar figures are placeholders and are not adopted.

The retrospective panel simulates 80, 90 and 100 eligible firms for FY 2024–25, FY 2025–26 and FY 2026–27 solely to demonstrate the requested historical-chart format. These counts do not describe what actually happened. The forward scenario assumes 10 additional eligible firms per year from a 100-firm baseline; it does not assume that Cortex Sentinel wins those firms.

At five seats per firm and ₹4,500 per device, each additional ten firms adds ₹2.25 lakh to the illustrative one-time device-value denominator. There is no replacement demand, subscription revenue or annual purchasing frequency inside this calculation. The actual historical size and growth of the narrowly defined target market remain unmeasured.

subsections.title: Differentiators (+ logic of their sustainability)
paragraphs: The intended distinction is a visible local workflow combining fingerprint permission with six workstation-environment checks before the product’s credential function proceeds. Planned controlled recovery gives that workflow a clearer restart/disconnect rule. These are intended design characteristics; customer value and comparative effectiveness remain unverified.

A credible advantage would have to come from dependable operation, customer-specific workflow understanding, usable recovery and consistent support. Component availability alone does not create defensibility: competitors can assemble similar parts, and customers already have alternative security layers. No patent, exclusive supply arrangement or proprietary advantage has been established.

subsections.title: Initiatives in Pipeline (with investment numbers, where possible)
paragraphs: First, verify two integrated devices and record faults, assembly time and delivered costs. Second, specify and test controlled recovery; its incremental engineering effort is not yet priced and must be checked against the pilot allowance before commitment. Third, complete the remaining eight only after the engineering gate.

Protected credential persistence, event history, mobile notifications and SIEM integration are deferred rather than silently included. Adding them requires a customer need, threat model, design effort and revised cost estimate. Gemini remains excluded.

subsections.title: Validation approach
paragraphs: Actual valid performance results are not yet available. Prior document test numbers were disclosed as made up and are not used as empirical evidence. The validation plan separates genuine and impostor biometric attempts, tests each of the six checks, measures false lockouts and detection delay, and records restart, disconnect, clipboard and credential-exposure limitations.

Any classroom example must carry the adjacent label “Illustrative example results — hypothetical, not measured.” A fictional zero false accepts in 50 impostor attempts is only a fictional sample proportion, not proof of a zero true false-acceptance rate.

subsections.title: Organization Structure
paragraphs: The five members are CS majors. Kavyansh coordinates the agreed workstreams; integration decisions, test findings and spending evidence should be reviewed together before releasing a milestone. Samarth maintains the cost and cash record, while Nitin preserves test protocols and raw outcomes.

These responsibilities have been accepted for planning. They do not establish individual qualifications, full-time availability, employment, compensation or ownership. Before commercial delivery, the team must check actual skills and hours, agree handoffs and obtain qualified assistance where hardware or security work exceeds its capability.

pages.title: IV) BUSINESS MODEL & FINANCIAL Plan
paragraphs: The business model begins with engineering validation, then a narrowly qualified customer evaluation, and only then potential commercial sales. A device sale and annual updates/support are the planned revenue categories. No sale is inferred from the ten engineering devices, and the pilot envelope does not fund ten years of operations.

The financial workbook covers 120 months from April 2027 to March 2037. It contains three illustrative cases and makes the principal risk visible: the base case loses money throughout the horizon. The accepted response is to improve validated economics, constrain spending or remain an engineering project, rather than present a forced profitable forecast.

subsections.title: Rollout plan
paragraphs: Year one prioritizes the two-unit engineering gate, five to eight exploratory conversations, cost measurement and any permitted limited evaluation. Years two and three depend on actual customer and operational evidence. Geographic expansion has no automatic date.

subsections.title: Financial Projections & Investment required
paragraphs: The teacher-directed request is framed around ₹44,470 of staged pilot resources. Award amount, terms and disbursement are unknown. The model separately illustrates recurring operating costs and unmet financing needs; those requirements are not secured facilities or an additional teacher ask.

subsections.title: Service economics
paragraphs: Base-case variable support uses one hour per paid account per year at ₹250/hour plus ₹50 of platform allowance: ₹300 cost and ₹200 annual contribution before fixed maintenance. The stress case costs ₹550 and loses ₹50 at the same retained fee; the lighter-support case costs ₹175. These are workload and rate assumptions, not measured operating results.

Annual service cash is billed upfront in the workbook and recognized over twelve months, leaving a visible future service obligation. A renewal is not assumed for customers who never existed; cohorts begin from new modeled sales.

subsections.title: Marketing Strategy: Promotion strategy, Online strategy
paragraphs: Begin with permission-based discovery and demonstrations of the defined workflow and limitations. An eventual online presence should explain compatibility, evidence, recovery and support terms rather than publish unverified protection claims. No campaign, website publication, institutional partnership or outreach has occurred.

An illustrative acquisition allocation of ₹8,000/month uses ₹6,000 already inside the ₹20,000 nonpay-overhead assumption plus eight hours already inside fixed operations at ₹250/hour. At one, two or four new paying firms, hypothetical CAC is ₹8,000, ₹4,000 or ₹2,000. Those denominators are sensitivity cases, not a conversion forecast; the allocation must not be charged again in the P&L.

subsections.title: Revenue model, costs and balance sheet drivers
paragraphs: Base assumptions: annual unit sales rise linearly from 24 to 240; assembly capacity is 20 devices/month; fixed operations are 40 hours/month at ₹250/hour, with ₹20,000/month other overhead. These are selected scenario mechanics, not researched sales growth or actual team commitments. Direct unit labor is already included in variable cost and is not duplicated in fixed operations.

The model separates customer receipts from revenue, core inventory purchases from expense, outstanding receivables, annual service obligations and financing gaps. It is pre-tax and uses constant FY 2027–28 purchasing power. Statutory tax, actual finance terms, full founder compensation and major redesign are unresolved exclusions, not claims that these costs are zero.

subsections.title: Key Matrices: break-even
paragraphs: Hardware-only monthly break-even = ceiling(fixed monthly cost ÷ positive device contribution). The base case requires ceiling(₹30,000 ÷ ₹1,053) = 29 devices/month, above its 20-device capacity. Nonpositive contribution has no finite unit break-even.

At twenty devices sold every month, hardware covers at most ₹21,060 of fixed monthly cost. Holding the other inputs fixed, covering ₹30,000 requires either ₹4,947 retained price or a ₹3,000 variable cost. These are single-driver thresholds, not attainable quotes, accepted prices or evidence of full-capacity sales.

pages.title: Thank you!
paragraphs: Cortex Sentinel seeks support for a disciplined engineering and customer-learning programme. The immediate decision is whether to resource the staged pilot, with spending linked to evidence and commercial expansion held behind product, customer and economic gates.

The team will report real test outcomes, including failures, maintain an auditable cost record and revise assumptions when evidence changes. A useful outcome may be a narrower product or a demonstrator rather than a commercial launch.
Prepared by Kavyansh Kumar Baghel, Manas Sharma, King Kapoor, Nitin Kumar and Samarth Jain.

subsections.title: Plan for 1 Yr
paragraphs: FY 2027–28: begin with two devices and documented power, logic-level, wiring, enclosure and functional checks. Prepare the five-to-eight-conversation discovery exercise, distinguish user/buyer/payer and obtain permission before any evaluation. Release the remaining eight only after the engineering gate. Before commercial builds, measure real assembly/support effort and test an actual price proposal.

Planning windows are Q1 engineering and discovery preparation, Q2 evidence review, Q3 a limited authorized evaluation if ready and Q4 an economic decision. These are conditional windows, not promised launch dates.

subsections.title: Plan for 3 Yrs
paragraphs: FY 2028–29 and FY 2029–30 develop only what real evidence supports. A learning path retains the project as a demonstrator if safe deployment, demand or affordable economics remain unresolved. A commercial path requires actual paying buyers, manageable service delivery and cash resources before repeat production. Wider India entry is considered only after repeatability; worldwide entry has no fixed date.

subsections.title: Operations Plan
paragraphs: Use the provisional CP2102 ESP32/R307/SH1106/driver/buzzer/Micro-B/PEM200 configuration as a planning BOM, not a verified assembly. Check UART voltage and possible level shifting, common ground, current peaks, I2C pullups, cable data capability and all physical openings before replication.

Keep setup, unit assembly labor, fulfillment and reserve separate. Accept each unit against a defined protocol, preserve failure records and provide controlled recovery instructions. A critical safety/security failure stops deployment until addressed.

subsections.title: Marketing Plan
paragraphs: Start with the approved accounting/finance SME discovery priority. Ask for current workflows, problems, existing alternatives, installation constraints and purchasing processes without leading respondents. Distinguish interview interest, permission for evaluation, a paid pilot and a repeat purchase.

Illustrative three-year service contribution is ₹438 per initially paid account at ₹200 annual contribution and 70% renewal. At 50% initial attach, that becomes ₹219 per sold device. It is a finite scenario calculation, not lifetime value or proof that customer acquisition is profitable.

pages.title: References and basis of preparation
paragraphs: External sources support narrowly described product offerings, listed prices and institutional context. Vendor statements are not independent comparative tests. Prices and stock may change; shipping, applicable tax treatment and compatibility require verification. The synthetic market counts and scenario sales are not derived from these sources.

Component prices [6–10] total ₹2,247; adding a ₹100 cable allowance gives ₹2,347. The remaining unit-cost lines are analyst allowances. No complete compatible-unit supplier quotation has been obtained.

The final plan is authorized for the classroom activity. The style-reference PDF is used for appearance only. User statements establish intended project choices, not empirical performance. The 23 teacher page requirements are preserved as ordered sections; substantive content may occupy additional physical pages.
